verdict: Bengaluru retains classic late-cycle froth signals — inventory building faster than absorption, launch mix heavily skewed to luxury, and wide asking-vs-guidance gaps in premium locales — but system-level shock absorbers (housing GNPA ~0.5%, EMI/income ~35%, stable repo at 5.25%) keep it out of distress. RBI MPC meets 3–5 Aug 2026; consensus is a hold, keeping typical home-loan rates around 8.0–8.5%. Composite tilt vs 19-Jul update: broadly unchanged.

indicators.name: Unsold inventory overhang
indicators.value: Bengaluru ~15 months (Q2 2026); pan-India unsold ~6.16 lakh units
indicators.note: Anarock Q2 2026: Bengaluru launches ~21,670 units (+41% YoY) vs sales ~15,285 units (+1% YoY); unsold stock ended 2025 at 64,863 units (+23% YoY). Anarock expects inventory to peak in Q3 2026 before festive absorption; Q3 2026 report not yet published. Overhang concentrated in East Bengaluru (Whitefield, Sarjapur).

indicators.name: Launch mix skew to luxury
indicators.note: Anarock Q2 2026 breakdown: ₹80L–1.5Cr = 27% of launches, ₹1.5–2.5Cr = 25%, above ₹2.5Cr = 22%. Only ~4% of supply catered to sub-₹80L buyers. Developers keep pivoting to premium as mid-segment demand thins. Unchanged since 19 Jul 2026 update.

indicators.name: EMI-to-income (affordability)
indicators.note: Knight Frank India Affordability Index H1 2026: Bengaluru EMI/income worsened marginally to 35% (from 34% in H2 2025) despite ~125 bps of cumulative easing. Home-loan rates now ~8.0–8.5% (typical ~8.25%). RBI held repo at 5.25% at June MPC; MPC meets again 3–5 Aug 2026 with consensus expecting a hold. Unchanged since 19 Jul 2026 update.
indicators.src: Knight Frank India Affordability Index H1 2026; RBI MPC June 2026

indicators.name: Housing-loan defaults (NPAs)
indicators.note: RBI Financial Stability Report June 2026: housing-loan GNPA at 0.5%; system GNPA at multi-decadal low 1.8%, projected to rise only to 1.9% by Mar 2028. CRAR 17.7%, CET1 15.3%. Secured retail GNPA 0.7%; unsecured retail 1.7% flagged for watch. Loans ≥₹50L now 44.7% of outstanding housing credit. Unchanged since 19 Jul 2026 update.

indicators.name: Asking vs registered price gap
indicators.note: Indiranagar guidance ~₹12k/sqft vs market ₹18–22k/sqft (50–83% premium). Newer corridors (Devanahalli, Hoskote) narrower at 15–25% and partially compressed after the Feb 2026 BBMP guidance hike (6–15%). A further statewide 10–20% guidance revision is under discussion for FY27 but not yet gazetted. Wide gap in prime pockets remains a clear froth signal.

indicators.name: Registration volumes
indicators.value: Karnataka FY25–26 stamps revenue ~₹20,837 cr (record); Kaveri 2.0 live; Jul 2026 monthly pending
indicators.note: Karnataka Stamps & Registration posted a record ~₹20,837 cr in FY25–26 (largely Bengaluru). Headline revenue is inflated by the Aug 2025 fee doubling (1%→2%) and Feb 2026 guidance hike — transactional volume growth is softer than revenue growth. Kaveri 2.0 fully live statewide (biometric-only in-person step); IGR Karnataka has not yet published monthly aggregates for Jul 2026.
